oidc_jwt.description: Reusing the same externally issued JWT may succeed until expiration because documentation only requires signature validation and exp freshness, not jti replay tracking.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay of the same JWT as a vulnerability without documented one-time-use semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: When a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
oidc_jwt.note: A token containing broad claims after an empty-scope request is by design, not an escalation bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive a refresh token when both the provider/application is configured for offline_access and the request includes the offline_access scope.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Authorization code / Refresh token grant
oidc_jwt.note: Missing refresh_token is expected unless offline_access is configured and requested.

oidc_jwt.description: A token can only be introspected from the same provider used to authenticate, unless first exchanged for a token from that provider.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-provider introspection failure is expected and should not be flagged as broken token handling.

oidc_jwt.description: The email_verified claim defaults to False in newer releases unless a custom scope mapping overrides it.
oidc_jwt.note: Applications expecting email_verified=true may fail by design; this is not identity corruption.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT-based machine-to-machine authentication creates service accounts derived from the provider name and JWT subject claim.
oidc_jwt.note: Granted identity names may differ from raw sub because authentik intentionally prefixes them with provider context.

oidc_jwt.description: Automatically generated service accounts for client_secret-based client_credentials follow the naming scheme ak-<provider_name>-client_credentials.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > Automatic service account creation
oidc_jwt.note: Provider-prefixed names are platform metadata, not necessarily identity mismatches.

oidc_jwt.description: RP-initiated logout normally ends only that application's session unless the default-provider-invalidation-flow is customized to include a User Logout stage.
oidc_jwt.source: User Logout stage; Single Logout docs
oidc_jwt.note: Remaining authentik session after app logout is by design unless full SLO is explicitly enabled.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly.
oidc_jwt.note: Second redemption failure is expected and should not be treated as a coherence bug.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 alg_none and resign_attacker_key tests against login_with_jwt, the fuzzer MUST configure JWT authentication by selecting trusted Federated OIDC Sources or Federated OIDC Providers first. Without that trust configuration, failures are ambiguous setup failures rather than proof-validation results.

For I1 trust_anchor_substitution and kid_injection tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST use a specific JWKS URL/raw JWKS on the OAuth Source or a specific federated provider selection. authentik fetches discovery/JWKS data on save and does no automatic re-fetching for OAuth Sources, so key-rotation and trust-anchor tests MUST explicitly re-save/update configuration before re-testing.

For I2 expired_token tests on externally issued JWTs, the attack token MUST set exp={{now_epoch_minus_N}} and the control token MUST set exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Documentation states external JWTs are rejected when exp is now or in the past.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti, do NOT report reuse of the same external JWT as a vulnerability by itself. The documentation only requires signature validation and exp freshness for external JWTs, and does not document jti tracking or one-time-use semantics.

For I2 tests on authentik-issued JWTs used as input to login_with_jwt, the token MUST first be revoked or expired when testing rejection. Documentation states authentik-issued input JWTs must be valid access tokens, must not have been revoked, and must not have expired.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation, after changing the OAuth Source Well-known URL, OIDC JWKS URL, or raw JWKS data, the fuzzer MUST trigger a save/update of that source before retrying login. Documentation states discovery/JWKS is fetched upon saving and no automatic re-fetching is done.

For I3 config-change sequences, NEW logins after admin configuration changes are expected to use the updated trust and policy configuration. A valid coherence test must compare behavior before and after the explicit reconfiguration, not treat changed behavior after save as a bug.

For I5 scope escalation tests, when no scope is requested authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. Therefore the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit limited scope set in baseline and attack requests; omitting scope invalidates least-privilege conclusions.

For I5 refresh-token and offline-access tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 a refresh token is only returned when both the application/provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping and the request includes scope=offline_access. Do NOT treat missing refresh_token without both conditions as a security bug.

For I5 scope authorization tests, additional scope restrictions are enforced via expression policies bound to the application, using request.context['oauth_scopes']. The fuzzer MUST configure such a policy if it wants scope-dependent allow/deny behavior; otherwise any configured scope is requestable by default.

For I5 empty_audience-style reasoning on OIDC access tokens, do NOT assume missing requested scope narrows claims unless explicit scopes are sent. By design, missing scope means all configured scopes are requested, except special scopes.

Redirect URI validation supports exact URIs and regex patterns configured by the administrator. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether the provider is configured with a literal URI or a regex. A regex match is by design and must not be flagged as a mismatch bypass.

For OIDC request object tests (oidc_request_object_alg_none), extract start_oidc_auth with optional request parameter, but the provided documentation does not state any request-object signature policy. Therefore failures or acceptance of unsigned request objects cannot be conclusively classified from these docs alone.

For introspection-based verification, the fuzzer MUST authenticate to the introspection endpoint with the same provider that issued the token, or first exchange the token into that provider. Documentation states a token can only be introspected from the same provider used to authenticate unless exchanged first.

The token endpoint /application/o/token/ is multiplexed across grant types. For oidc_jwt tests, the fuzzer MUST set grant_type explicitly for each scenario: authorization_code for code exchange, client_credentials for M2M, urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code for device flow polling, and refresh_token for refresh. Missing or wrong grant_type causes misleading failures unrelated to the invariant under test.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs; Device code flow docs; Machine-to-machine docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 JWT-signature tests against login_with_jwt, the fuzzer MUST first configure the target OAuth2 provider to trust either Federated OIDC Sources or Federated OIDC Providers. Without that trust configuration, all JWT assertion logins fail trivially and do not test signature/key validation behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-machine authentication -> Externally issued JWTs / authentik-issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 trust-anchor-substitution and key-rotation tests, note that authentik fetches OIDC discovery/JWKS data when the source is saved and performs no automatic re-fetching. A valid key-rotation test MUST include re-saving/updating the source/provider trust configuration after changing the upstream JWKS; otherwise stale cached keys may be used and results will be misinterpreted.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source -> Well-known: 'This URL is fetched upon saving the source... No automatic re-fetching is done.'

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token tests on login_with_jwt, authentik explicitly checks that the input JWT exp is not now or in the past. The fuzzer SHOULD use a control token with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and an attack token with exp={{now_epoch_minus_60}} to distinguish correct expiry enforcement from broken setup.

For I2 future_token/nbf tests on login_with_jwt, the provided docs only explicitly mention exp validation for externally issued JWTs and do not document nbf handling. The fuzzer MUST treat nbf behavior as undocumented and include a valid control token in the same campaign; do not classify nbf acceptance/rejection as a documentation contradiction without empirical confirmation.

For I2 replay_same_token against login_with_jwt, do NOT flag reuse of the same externally issued JWT as a vulnerability by default. The docs describe stateless JWT acceptance based on signature trust and expiry, not one-time-use tracking. Replay resistance is only documented for authentik-issued access tokens insofar as they must not be revoked and must not have expired.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-machine authentication -> Externally issued JWTs / authentik-issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 config-change sequences involving OAuth/OIDC sources embedded in flows, source-stage resume is time-bound. If the configured Resume timeout is exceeded, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning. The fuzzer MUST keep multi-step source-based sequences within the resume timeout or else apparent flow incoherence may be by design.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, authentik validates redirect URIs against the provider's configured Redirect URI list. Redirect URIs may be exact values or regexes. The fuzzer MUST know whether the provider under test was configured with an exact URI or a regex; a mismatch that still matches the configured regex is BY DESIGN and not a vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 authorization-code replay tests, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. The fuzzer SHOULD test same-code reuse directly at /application/o/token/ and interpret second-use failure as expected behavior.

For I3 PKCE tests, the token endpoint accepts code_verifier when supplied, but the docs do not state that PKCE is mandatory for all clients. The fuzzer MUST treat PKCE enforcement as configuration-dependent hardening, not assume universal rejection when code_verifier is omitted unless the authorization request actually included a code_challenge.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs; Device code/M2M context fields mention oauth_code_verifier

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I4 identity-collision tests on login_with_jwt, authentik creates service accounts for JWT authentication using a naming scheme based on provider name and the token subject claim. The fuzzer MUST compare granted identity against subject-derived service-account naming, not expect a human user object. Different providers can legitimately prefix identities differently.

For I4 cross-provider identity tests, authentik can create multiple service accounts depending on the tokens provided, and service accounts are based on provider name plus subject claim. The fuzzer MUST vary provider/application context separately from sub when testing cross-mount or cross-provider collisions, because provider name is part of the intended identity namespace.

For I5 scope-binding tests, when no scopes are requested authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested, except for special scopes. Therefore the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope string in baseline and attack requests. Omitting scope broadens claims by design and will create false positives for over-grant tests.

For I5 refresh-token and offline-access tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 applications only receive a refresh token when both the application/provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping and the request includes the offline_access scope. The fuzzer MUST configure and request offline_access together; otherwise missing refresh_token is expected.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Authorization code / Refresh token grant / Create OAuth2 provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 token introspection tests, authentik only allows introspection of a token from the same provider used to authenticate, unless the token is first exchanged for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection requests with the matching provider context or perform token exchange first; cross-provider introspection failure is by design.

For I5 token-exchange audience/scope tests, the provided docs do not explicitly document RFC 8693 token exchange semantics for audience restriction on subject_token. The fuzzer SHOULD still test audience and scope narrowing empirically at /application/o/token/, but MUST treat failures to exchange across providers as potentially due to provider-scoped token validity rather than a direct audience-binding check.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider endpoint table; Machine-to-machine authentication introspection/provider-scoping notes

oidc_jwt.constraint: User Login stage session duration has a documented sentinel: seconds=0 means the authentik session expires when the browser is closed, not an arbitrary positive TTL. Stay signed in offset also defaults to seconds=0 meaning disabled/no extension prompt. Never assume 0 means 'use platform default nonzero lifetime'.

Authenticator Validation stage last validation threshold has a documented sentinel: zero means MFA validation is required every time; any non-zero value enables less-frequent validation. Never assume 0 disables validation entirely.

Email authenticator Token Expiration is documented in minutes with default 30. No disable sentinel is documented. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables expiry or selects a default unless verified separately.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti tests, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT in login_with_jwt as a vulnerability by itself. The documentation describes JWT authentication as accepting valid externally issued JWTs or authentik-issued access tokens and does not document jti replay tracking for JWT bearer authentication; only expiry/revocation checks are documented.

For I2 expired_token tests against login_with_jwt, include a control login using a valid JWT with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. authentik explicitly checks that external input JWT exp is not now or in the past, and authentik-issued JWTs must not have expired. Without a control, a generic token error cannot be distinguished from broken provider/source setup.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > Externally issued JWTs / authentik-issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 future_token tests, the provided docs only explicitly document exp validation for external JWT login and do not explicitly document nbf handling for login_with_jwt. The fuzzer SHOULD still test nbf/future-token behavior, but MUST interpret failures carefully because documentation does not guarantee nbf enforcement semantics.

For I1 trust-anchor and key-rotation tests on login_with_jwt, the fuzzer MUST first configure the OAuth2 provider to trust specific Federated OIDC Sources or Federated OIDC Providers. JWT login succeeds for any JWT signed by any configured source/provider certificate; without explicit trust setup, issuer/key-substitution tests are meaningless.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > Externally issued JWTs / authentik-issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, authentik does not document a built-in exact issuer binding parameter on the JWT login endpoint. To enforce issuer restrictions, the fuzzer MUST use an Expression policy over request.context["oauth_jwt"]["iss"]. Do NOT assume issuer is checked merely because signature trust is configured.

For I5 scope tests, when no scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. Therefore, to test least-privilege or scope escalation, the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope value and MUST NOT omit scope expecting minimal/default access.

For I5 refresh-token expectations, starting with authentik 2024.2 applications only receive a refresh token when both the application/provider is configured with offline_access scope mapping and the request includes offline_access. Do NOT flag missing refresh_token as a bug unless both conditions are satisfied.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider > Authorization code / Refresh token grant / Create OAuth2 provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 authorization-code coherence tests, authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly by design. Reuse of the same code should be treated as expected rejection, not as a session-binding bug. State/code swap tests must compare cross-session misuse, not simple second redemption of the same code.

For I3 PKCE tests, authentik documentation states support for PKCE but does not state that PKCE is mandatory for all clients. The fuzzer MUST evaluate pkce_skip and related checks via token-endpoint HTTP status/error behavior only, and MUST NOT infer identity confusion from a rejected or accepted exchange without client-type context.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, redirect URIs are validated against the provider's configured Redirect URI list, and the field may contain regex patterns. The fuzzer MUST know whether the configured redirect URI entry is literal or regex-based; a match caused by admin-configured regex is by design, not a mismatch bypass.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider > Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Numeric sentinel: in User Login stage, Session duration default seconds=0 means browser-session cookie expiry, not an immediately expired session. Stay signed in offset default seconds=0 means no extension prompt. Remember device only activates when set above 0. Never assume 0 disables authentication or means token instantly expires.

Numeric sentinel: Authenticator Validation stage Last validation threshold default/non-zero semantics matter. A value of 0 means MFA validation is required every time; any non-zero value enables reuse of prior validation within that window. Never assume 0 means 'use default cache'.

Numeric sentinel: Email Authenticator Setup stage Token Expiration is in minutes and defaults to 30. Tests for one-time email-code freshness must account for this default if the stage is used in the underlying flow.

For I3 config-change sequences, any change to provider/source configuration is expected to affect NEW logins immediately. A valid coherence test must show stale acceptance of old trust/config after reconfiguration, not merely that behavior changed after an admin update.
oidc_jwt.source: Outposts overview (changes trigger immediate update) and OAuth/JWT configuration docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, exchanged-token claims are influenced by requested scopes and provider scope mappings. Because omitted scope means all configured scopes, the baseline token and exchanged token MUST both use explicit scope values so claim expansion can be attributed to token exchange rather than default-scope behavior.

For I5 token introspection tests, the docs state you can only introspect a token from the same provider used to authenticate, or after exchanging it into that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection requests with the matching provider context; cross-provider introspection failure is by design.

For I4 identity-collision tests on JWT login, authentik creates service accounts based on the provider name and the subject claim of the input token. Tests must vary sub while keeping provider constant to probe collision behavior; cross-provider differences may legitimately produce different service-account namespaces.

For I4 cross-mount/cross-provider collision tests, service-account naming and identity creation are provider-scoped. The fuzzer MUST distinguish collisions within the same provider from identities created under different providers, because provider name participates in service-account naming.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication > Automatic service account creation / JWT authentication

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience tests on token exchange or JWT login, the provided docs do not document a dedicated exact-match audience restriction parameter on the login endpoint. Audience/claim restrictions must be implemented via policies over request.context["oauth_jwt"] or provider/application configuration. Do NOT invent wildcard audience semantics from other products.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication and OAuth2 provider docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 claim-type coercion tests, the docs expose parsed JWT claims to Expression policies as a dictionary in request.context["oauth_jwt"]. Because no claim-matching mode parameter is documented, the fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly in policy logic scenarios (e.g., integer bound vs float claim) and MUST NOT assume wildcard/glob matching support exists for claims.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
